docs.title: Write once, deploy to any supported cloud
docs.text:
MultiCloud-Py is a cloud-agnostic Python SDK providing unified interfaces for cloud services. Build applications against a consistent API and select a cloud provider when you create a client.

Get started API reference

docs.title: Key features
docs.text:
• Cloud-agnostic APIs: use the same client interface across supported providers.
  • Provider isolation: install only the service and provider packages you need.
  • Native cloud SDKs: provider implementations use the underlying cloud SDKs.
  • Consistent errors: handle a shared exception hierarchy in application code.
  • Conformance tests: shared tests verify behavior across provider implementations.

docs.title: One API across clouds
docs.text:
from multicloud.blob.blob_client import BucketClient

with BucketClient(provider="aws", bucket="my-bucket", region="us-west-2") as client:
    client.upload(key="hello.txt", payload=b"Hello, MultiCloud-Py!")
    response = client.download(key="hello.txt")
    print(response.content)

Select provider="gcp" and use your Cloud Storage bucket and region to run the same operations on GCP. Configure credentials for the selected provider before running the example.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: Use Python 3.10 or newer. Install only the service and provider packages your application needs; they bring in the shared client and common dependencies.

docs.title: Install a provider
docs.text:
Once the distributions are available on PyPI:

# Blob Storage on AWS
pip install multicloud-py-blob-aws

# Blob Storage on GCP
pip install multicloud-py-blob-gcp

For development from source, install the workspace with uv:

git clone https://github.com/salesforce/multicloud-py.git
cd multicloud-py
uv sync --frozen --all-packages

Run examples from the source checkout with uv run python example.py.

docs.title: Configure access
docs.text:
Create a bucket and grant your identity permission to upload, download, and delete objects in it. Use a bucket intended for trying the SDK.

AWSGCP

Configure the standard boto3 credential chain, such as an AWS profile, environment credentials, or a workload role. Use the bucket's region.

Configure Application Default Credentials, such as a workload identity or gcloud auth application-default login for local development. Use your Cloud Storage bucket and location.

docs.title: Upload and download an object
docs.text:
Replace my-bucket and the region with your own values. This example writes and then deletes multicloud-py-getting-started.txt.

from multicloud.blob.blob_client import BucketClient

with BucketClient(provider="aws", bucket="my-bucket", region="us-west-2") as client:
    key = "multicloud-py-getting-started.txt"
    client.upload(key=key, payload=b"Hello, MultiCloud-Py!")
    response = client.download(key=key)
    print(response.content.decode())
    client.delete(key=key)

To use GCP, install multicloud-py-blob-gcp, select provider="gcp", and provide your bucket and location. The upload, download, and delete calls stay the same.

docs.title: multicloud.blob
docs.text: Cloud-agnostic object storage. The user-facing entry points are BucketClient (sync) and AsyncBucketClient (async).

docs.title: Sync API
docs.text:
Cloud-agnostic blob client package.

Public entry point — :class:BucketClient::

from multicloud.blob.blob_client import BucketClient

with BucketClient(
    provider="aws", bucket="my-bucket", region="us-west-2"
) as client:
    client.upload("hello.txt", b"hi")
    resp = client.download("hello.txt")
    client.delete("hello.txt")

Switch clouds by changing the provider kwarg only::

BucketClient(provider="gcp", bucket="my-bucket", region="us-central1")

Provider classes (AwsBlobStore, GcpBlobStore, ...) live in sibling distributions (multicloud-blob-aws, -gcp, -ali) and are discovered at runtime via setuptools entry points. They are hidden behind the registry; users never reference them directly.

download_stream(
    key: str,
    *,
    version_id: Optional[str] = None,
    start: Optional[int] = None,
    end: Optional[int] = None
) -> StreamingDownloadResponse

Download the object as a streaming response for lazy consumption.

Returns a streaming response that yields content on demand without loading the entire blob into memory. The caller must close the response (preferably via a context manager) to release the underlying HTTP connection.

Conditional reads (if_match) are supported on download() only; use it when you need an ETag precondition.

Example::

with client.download_stream("large-file.bin") as stream:
    for chunk in stream:
        process(chunk)

delete_directory(
    prefix: Optional[str],
    *,
    max_concurrency: int = DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENCY
) -> None

Delete all objects under a prefix asynchronously.

Deletes every object whose key begins with the prefix. Deletes are parallelized using asyncio with bounded concurrency. A prefix matching no objects is a successful no-op, and objects already absent count as deleted.

The prefix is matched verbatim and is never normalized, so a prefix without a trailing "/" also matches sibling keys sharing its leading characters -- "logs" matches "logs.txt" and "logs-archive/x" as well as "logs/x". Pass a trailing "/" to target only the directory.

Warning

An empty or None prefix matches every object in the bucket and deletes all of them.

Only the current version of each object is deleted, so on a version-enabled bucket earlier versions are retained and storage is not necessarily reclaimed. The operation is not atomic: objects written under the prefix while it runs may survive.

docs.title: Provider registry
docs.text:
Provider discovery registry.

A small in-process registry keyed by provider id (e.g. "aws", "gcp"). Provider classes register themselves with the @registry.register("aws") decorator at import time; the user-facing client (e.g. BucketClient) looks up the right class by id at construction time.

This is a service-locator pattern — it emerges when a single API must dispatch to multiple backend implementations at runtime.

Provider modules in this SDK are loaded lazily from setuptools entry points. Each provider distribution declares an entry point in the multicloud.<svc>.providers group; :meth:ProviderRegistry.discover imports those modules on the first :meth:ProviderRegistry.get call so the @register decorators run and the providers become resolvable.

Override the default credentials resolution.

Modeled as a grouped configuration object because its fields are interdependent and validated as a unit — the required subset of fields changes based on credentials_type.

Used when a service needs to: 1. Supply explicit session credentials (SESSION) 2. Assume a role from another account (ASSUME_ROLE) 3. Exchange a web identity token for credentials (ASSUME_ROLE_WEB_IDENTITY)

docs.title: SignedAuthRequest dataclass
docs.text:
SignedAuthRequest(
    method: str,
    url: str,
    headers: Mapping[str, str],
    body: bytes,
    credentials: StsCredentials,
)

A signed-but-unsent identity request.

Produced by :meth:BaseStsUtilities.create_signed_auth_request. The caller forwards the request itself — method, url, headers, and body — to an identity broker, which replays it to the provider to prove the caller's identity.

Security: this is a replayable identity proof — the signed headers (and any session token on credentials) let anyone holding them impersonate the signer until the signature expires. Treat it as a secret: __repr__ redacts the sensitive parts, but dataclasses.asdict and direct field access do not.

  • method: HTTP method of the signed request
  • url: fully-qualified request URL
  • headers: signed request headers; redacted in repr
  • body: request body bytes
  • credentials: non-secret signer identity (key id + session token); the long-term signing secret is omitted

docs.title: Design Documentation
docs.text: Architecture and design decisions for the Python Multi-Cloud SDK.

docs.title: Topics
docs.text:
• Layers — The three-layer architecture (Client, Driver, Provider)
  • Exception Handling — Common exception hierarchy and error translation

docs.title: Exception Handling
docs.text: The SDK provides a unified exception hierarchy so that user code can write a single except clause that works across all cloud providers.

docs.title: Exception Hierarchy
docs.text:
SubstrateSdkException (root)
├── InvalidArgumentException
├── ResourceNotFoundException
├── ResourceExistsException
├── UnAuthorizedException
├── FailedPreconditionException
├── UnsupportedOperationException
└── UnknownException

All exceptions are defined in multicloud.common.exceptions.

docs.title: Exception Types
docs.text: Exception HTTP Analog When Raised InvalidArgumentException 400 Caller provided invalid input (empty key, bad type) ResourceNotFoundException 404 Target resource (bucket, object, role) does not exist ResourceExistsException 409 Attempted to create a resource that already exists UnAuthorizedException 401/403 Credentials missing, expired, or insufficient permissions FailedPreconditionException 412 Operation rejected because a precondition was not met UnsupportedOperationException 501 Operation not supported by this provider UnknownException 500 Catch-all for errors that do not map to a specific type

docs.title: Error Translation Pattern
docs.text:
Every provider must implement translate_error() — an instance method that maps native SDK exceptions to the common hierarchy:

class AwsBlobStore(BaseBlobStore):
    def translate_error(self, exc: Exception) -> SubstrateSdkException:
        """Translate AWS SDK exceptions to common hierarchy."""
        if isinstance(exc, SubstrateSdkException):
            return exc  # Already translated
        if isinstance(exc, ClientError):
            code = exc.response["Error"]["Code"]
            if code in ("NoSuchBucket", "NoSuchKey"):
                return ResourceNotFoundException(str(exc))
            if code == "AccessDenied":
                return UnAuthorizedException(str(exc))
            if code == "BucketAlreadyOwnedByYou":
                return ResourceExistsException(str(exc))
        if isinstance(exc, NoCredentialsError):
            return UnAuthorizedException(str(exc))
        return UnknownException(str(exc))

docs.title: Key Rules
docs.text:
1. Instance method — translate_error(self, exc) is enforced via @abstractmethod on the Provider base class
  2. Preserve the original exception — Always use raise translated from exc
  3. Service-specific mappings — Blob error codes differ from STS error codes, so each service's providers implement their own translation
  4. Check if already translated — Return exc unchanged if it's already a SubstrateSdkException

docs.title: Usage in Provider Hooks
docs.text:
Providers catch native exceptions in their do_* methods and translate them:

class AwsBlobStore(BaseBlobStore):
    def do_upload(self, key, payload, **kwargs):
        try:
            self._s3.put_object(Bucket=self.bucket, Key=key, Body=payload)
        except (ClientError, BotoCoreError) as exc:
            raise self.translate_error(exc) from exc
        return UploadResponse(key=key, ...)

docs.title: User-Facing Error Handling
docs.text:
Users catch exceptions from the common hierarchy — never provider-specific exceptions:

from multicloud.blob import BucketClient
from multicloud.common.exceptions import (
    ResourceNotFoundException,
    UnAuthorizedException,
    SubstrateSdkException,
)

with BucketClient(provider="aws", bucket="b", region="us-west-2") as client:
    try:
        client.download("missing-key.txt")
    except ResourceNotFoundException:
        print("Object not found")
    except UnAuthorizedException:
        print("Access denied — check credentials")
    except SubstrateSdkException:
        print("Other SDK error")

docs.title: Input Validation
docs.text:
Input validation happens at Layer 2 (Driver) before the provider hook is called. Validation errors raise InvalidArgumentException:

# In BaseBlobStore.upload():
if not key or not key.strip():
    raise InvalidArgumentException("key must be a non-empty string")

This ensures consistent validation regardless of which provider is in use.

docs.title: Three-Layer Architecture
docs.text: Every service in the Python Multi-Cloud SDK follows a strict three-layer architecture that separates concerns between user-facing API, abstract contracts, and cloud-specific implementations.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
User code
  │
  ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Layer 1 — Client                   │  BucketClient, StsClient
│  (Public API, cloud-agnostic)       │
└───────────────┬─────────────────────┘
                │ delegates to
                ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Layer 2 — Driver                   │  BaseBlobStore, BaseSts
│  (Abstract contract + validation)   │
└───────────────┬─────────────────────┘
                │ calls do_* hooks
                ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Layer 3 — Provider                 │  AwsBlobStore, GcpBlobStore, AwsSts
│  (Cloud-specific implementation)    │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Layer 1 — Client
docs.text:
Purpose: User-facing, cloud-agnostic entry point.

Examples: BucketClient, StsClient

Responsibilities: - Accept provider keyword argument and resolve the implementation via the registry - Forward calls to the driver (Layer 2) - Manage lifecycle (__enter__ / __exit__ / close()) - Never import from provider packages

from multicloud.blob import BucketClient

with BucketClient(provider="aws", bucket="my-bucket", region="us-west-2") as client:
    client.upload("key", b"data")

docs.title: Layer 2 — Driver
docs.text:
Purpose: Abstract contract defining the public method signatures, input validation, and template-method hooks.

Examples: BaseBlobStore, BaseSts

Responsibilities: - Define public methods (upload, download, delete) as concrete methods - Validate inputs via a Validator class - Normalize arguments (defaults, coercion) - Delegate to abstract do_* hooks that providers implement - Own the registry instance (BLOB_REGISTRY, STS_REGISTRY) - Define frozen dataclasses for request/response types

class BaseBlobStore(Provider, ABC):
    def upload(self, key, payload, *, content_type=None, ...):
        # 1. Validate input
        self._validator.validate_upload(key)
        # 2. Normalize
        payload_bytes = _coerce_to_bytes(payload)
        # 3. Delegate to provider hook
        return self.do_upload(key, payload_bytes, content_type=content_type, ...)

    @abstractmethod
    def do_upload(self, key, payload, *, content_type=None, ...) -> UploadResponse:
        ...

docs.title: Layer 3 — Provider
docs.text:
Purpose: Concrete, cloud-specific implementation.

Examples: AwsBlobStore, GcpBlobStore, AwsSts, GcpSts

Responsibilities: - Override do_* hooks only (never override upload/download/delete) - Use the native cloud SDK (boto3, google-cloud-storage, etc.) - Implement translate_error() to map native exceptions to the common hierarchy - Self-register at import time via the @REGISTRY.register("provider_id") decorator

@BLOB_REGISTRY.register("aws")
class AwsBlobStore(BaseBlobStore):
    def do_upload(self, key, payload, *, content_type=None, ...):
        try:
            self._s3.put_object(Bucket=self.bucket, Key=key, Body=payload, ...)
        except (ClientError, BotoCoreError) as exc:
            raise self.translate_error(exc) from exc
        return UploadResponse(key=key, e_tag=..., version_id=...)

    def translate_error(self, exc):
        if isinstance(exc, ClientError):
            code = exc.response["Error"]["Code"]
            if code in ("NoSuchBucket", "NoSuchKey"):
                return ResourceNotFoundException(str(exc))
        return UnknownException(str(exc))

docs.title: Provider Discovery
docs.text:
Each service owns a ProviderRegistry instance. Providers self-register at import time:

# In blob_client/driver.py
BLOB_REGISTRY = ProviderRegistry(service_name="blob")

# In blob_aws/aws_blob_store.py
@BLOB_REGISTRY.register("aws")
class AwsBlobStore(BaseBlobStore):
    ...

The service triggers registration with guarded imports (at the bottom of driver.py or in the service __init__.py):

# Guarded import triggers @BLOB_REGISTRY.register("aws") decorator
try:
    from multicloud.blob import blob_aws  # noqa: F401
except ImportError as _exc:
    BLOB_REGISTRY.record_import_error("aws", _exc)

docs.title: Dependency Rules
docs.text:
Layer May Import Must NOT Import Client sibling driver any provider package Driver multicloud.common.* any provider package Provider sibling driver, multicloud.common.*, native SDKs other provider packages

These rules guarantee that: - User code never sees provider classes - Providers cannot depend on each other - The client/driver layers remain fully cloud-agnostic

docs.title: Package Layout
docs.text:
Every service follows the same 3-package structure:

multicloud/<svc>/
├── <svc>_client/        # Layer 1 + Layer 2
│   ├── client.py        # User-facing Client class
│   └── driver.py        # BaseFoo + registry + dataclasses
├── <svc>_aws/           # Layer 3: AWS provider
├── <svc>_gcp/           # Layer 3: GCP provider
└── <svc>_ali/           # Layer 3: Ali provider

docs.title: Blob Storage Guide
docs.text: The Blob Storage service provides cloud-agnostic object storage operations — upload, download, and delete objects across AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, and Ali OSS.

docs.title: Creating a Client
docs.text:
BucketClient is scoped to a single bucket. All operations target that bucket.

from multicloud.blob import BucketClient

# AWS S3
with BucketClient(provider="aws", bucket="my-bucket", region="us-west-2") as client:
    ...

# Google Cloud Storage
with BucketClient(provider="gcp", bucket="my-bucket", region="us-central1") as client:
    ...

docs.title: Constructor Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Description provider str ✅ Provider id: "aws", "gcp", or "ali" bucket str ✅ Bucket name region str Region (AWS region / GCS location) endpoint str Endpoint URL override

All parameters are keyword-only (enforced by * separator).

Note

Credentials are discovered automatically from environment variables, config files, or IAM/ADC. The SDK never accepts explicit credential parameters.

docs.title: Uploading Objects
docs.text:
from multicloud.blob import BucketClient

with BucketClient(provider="aws", bucket="my-bucket", region="us-west-2") as client:
    # Upload raw bytes
    resp = client.upload("hello.txt", b"Hello, World!")
    print(f"Uploaded: {resp.key}, ETag: {resp.e_tag}")

    # Upload with metadata and content type
    resp = client.upload(
        "data.json",
        b'{"key": "value"}',
        content_type="application/json",
        metadata={"author": "sdk-user", "version": "1"},
    )

docs.title: Upload from a File
docs.text:
with BucketClient(provider="aws", bucket="my-bucket", region="us-west-2") as client:
    with open("large-file.bin", "rb") as f:
        resp = client.upload("backups/large-file.bin", f)

docs.title: Upload Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description key str ✅ Object key (path) in the bucket payload bytes \| BinaryIO ✅ Content to upload content_type str MIME type (e.g., "text/plain") content_length int Size in bytes (auto-detected if omitted) metadata Mapping[str, str] User-defined metadata

docs.title: UploadResponse
docs.text:
UploadResponse is a frozen dataclass:

Field Type Description key str Object key e_tag str \| None Entity tag (content hash) version_id str \| None Version ID (if versioning enabled)

docs.title: Downloading Objects
docs.text:
with BucketClient(provider="aws", bucket="my-bucket", region="us-west-2") as client:
    resp = client.download("hello.txt")
    print(f"Content: {resp.content.decode()}")
    print(f"Content-Type: {resp.metadata.content_type}")
    print(f"Size: {resp.metadata.content_length} bytes")

docs.title: Range Downloads
docs.text:
Download a specific byte range:

with BucketClient(provider="aws", bucket="my-bucket", region="us-west-2") as client:
    # Download bytes 0–99 (first 100 bytes)
    resp = client.download("large-file.bin", start=0, end=99)

docs.title: Download with Version
docs.text:
with BucketClient(provider="aws", bucket="my-bucket", region="us-west-2") as client:
    resp = client.download("hello.txt", version_id="abc123")

docs.title: Download Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description key str ✅ Object key version_id str Specific version to download start int Start byte for range download (inclusive) end int End byte for range download (inclusive)

docs.title: DownloadResponse
docs.text:

Field Type Description key str Object key content bytes Downloaded content metadata BlobMetadata Object metadata (see below)

docs.title: BlobMetadata
docs.text:
Nested within DownloadResponse.metadata:

Field Type Description key str Object key content_length int \| None Size in bytes content_type str \| None MIME type e_tag str \| None Entity tag version_id str \| None Version ID metadata Mapping[str, str] User-defined metadata

docs.title: Deleting Objects
docs.text:
with BucketClient(provider="aws", bucket="my-bucket", region="us-west-2") as client:
    client.delete("hello.txt")

Delete is idempotent — deleting a non-existent key does not raise an error.

docs.title: Multipart Uploads
docs.text:
Large objects can be uploaded in parts. Initiate a session, upload each part, then complete to assemble the final object:

from multicloud.blob import BucketClient, MultipartPart

with BucketClient(provider="aws", bucket="my-bucket", region="us-west-2") as client:
    mpu = client.initiate_multipart_upload("big-file.bin", content_type="application/octet-stream")

    parts = []
    parts.append(client.upload_part(mpu, MultipartPart(part_number=1, content=chunk_1)))
    parts.append(client.upload_part(mpu, MultipartPart(part_number=2, content=chunk_2)))

    client.complete_multipart_upload(mpu, parts)

docs.title: Object Lock at Initiate
docs.text:
Pass object_lock to initiate_multipart_upload to apply retention and/or a legal hold to the final assembled object. The lock is set on the object produced when the upload completes:

from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

from multicloud.blob import (
    BucketClient,
    MultipartPart,
    ObjectLockConfiguration,
    RetentionMode,
)

with BucketClient(provider="aws", bucket="my-bucket", region="us-west-2") as client:
    lock = ObjectLockConfiguration(
        mode=RetentionMode.GOVERNANCE,
        retain_until_date=datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(days=7),
        legal_hold=True,
    )
    mpu = client.initiate_multipart_upload("locked-file.bin", object_lock=lock)

    part = client.upload_part(mpu, MultipartPart(part_number=1, content=payload))
    client.complete_multipart_upload(mpu, [part])

    # The lock is present on the completed object:
    info = client.get_object_lock("locked-file.bin")
    print(info.mode, info.retain_until_date, info.legal_hold)

ObjectLockConfiguration fields:

Field Type Description mode RetentionMode GOVERNANCE or COMPLIANCE; requires retain_until_date retain_until_date datetime Timezone-aware instant until which the object is retained; requires mode legal_hold bool Place a legal hold on the object use_event_based_hold bool Apply a requested legal hold as an event-based hold where the provider distinguishes the two

Note

GOVERNANCE retention can be shortened or removed by sufficiently privileged callers; COMPLIANCE retention cannot be shortened or removed by anyone until it expires. A retained object cannot be deleted until its retention expires (or is shortened, for GOVERNANCE), and an object under legal hold cannot be deleted until the hold is released.

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
A full round-trip: upload, download, verify, delete.

from multicloud.blob import BucketClient

with BucketClient(provider="aws", bucket="my-bucket", region="us-west-2") as client:
    # Upload
    upload_resp = client.upload(
        "test/round-trip.txt",
        b"round-trip content",
        content_type="text/plain",
        metadata={"purpose": "testing"},
    )
    print(f"Uploaded: {upload_resp.key}")

    # Download and verify
    download_resp = client.download("test/round-trip.txt")
    assert download_resp.content == b"round-trip content"
    assert download_resp.metadata.metadata["purpose"] == "testing"

    # Cleanup
    client.delete("test/round-trip.txt")
    print("Deleted successfully")

docs.title: Switching Providers
docs.text:
The same code works across clouds — change only the provider and region:

from multicloud.blob import BucketClient

providers = [
    {"provider": "aws", "bucket": "my-aws-bucket", "region": "us-west-2"},
    {"provider": "gcp", "bucket": "my-gcp-bucket", "region": "us-central1"},
]

for config in providers:
    with BucketClient(**config) as client:
        client.upload("hello.txt", b"same code, different cloud")
        resp = client.download("hello.txt")
        print(f"[{config['provider']}] Content: {resp.content.decode()}")
        client.delete("hello.txt")

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
All blob operations raise exceptions from the common multicloud.common.exceptions hierarchy:

from multicloud.blob import BucketClient
from multicloud.common.exceptions import (
    ResourceNotFoundException,
    InvalidArgumentException,
    UnAuthorizedException,
    SubstrateSdkException,
)

with BucketClient(provider="aws", bucket="my-bucket", region="us-west-2") as client:
    try:
        resp = client.download("does-not-exist.txt")
    except ResourceNotFoundException as e:
        print(f"Object not found: {e}")
    except UnAuthorizedException as e:
        print(f"Access denied: {e}")
    except SubstrateSdkException as e:
        print(f"SDK error: {e}")
Exception When Raised ResourceNotFoundException Object or bucket does not exist InvalidArgumentException Empty key, invalid content_type, bad range UnAuthorizedException Credentials missing, expired, or insufficient ResourceExistsException Duplicate resource on create UnknownException Unmapped provider error

docs.title: Client Lifecycle
docs.text:
BucketClient supports the context manager protocol:

# Preferred — automatic cleanup
with BucketClient(provider="aws", bucket="b", region="us-west-2") as client:
    client.upload("key", b"data")

# Manual cleanup
client = BucketClient(provider="aws", bucket="b", region="us-west-2")
try:
    client.upload("key", b"data")
finally:
    client.close()

docs.title: Pub/Sub Guide
docs.text: The Pub/Sub service provides cloud-agnostic publish-subscribe messaging — send messages to topics and receive them from subscriptions across AWS SNS/SQS, Google Cloud Pub/Sub, and Ali MNS.

docs.title: Topic Client
docs.text:
TopicClient is scoped to a single topic. All operations target that topic.

from multicloud.pubsub import TopicClient

# AWS SNS
with TopicClient(provider="aws", topic_name="orders", region="us-west-2") as client:
    ...

# Google Cloud Pub/Sub
with TopicClient(provider="gcp", topic_name="orders", region="us-central1") as client:
    ...

docs.title: Subscription Client
docs.text:
SubscriptionClient is scoped to a single subscription. All operations target that subscription.

from multicloud.pubsub import SubscriptionClient

# AWS SQS
with SubscriptionClient(provider="aws", subscription_name="orders-processor", region="us-west-2") as client:
    ...

# Google Cloud Pub/Sub
with SubscriptionClient(provider="gcp", subscription_name="orders-processor", region="us-central1") as client:
    ...

docs.title: Constructor Parameters
docs.text:
TopicClient:

Parameter Type Required Description provider str ✅ Provider id: "aws", "gcp", or "ali" topic_name str ✅ Topic name region str Region/location endpoint str Endpoint URL override

SubscriptionClient:

Parameter Type Required Description provider str ✅ Provider id: "aws", "gcp", or "ali" subscription_name str ✅ Subscription name region str Region/location endpoint str Endpoint URL override nack_visibility_timeout timedelta Default visibility timeout for nacks

All parameters are keyword-only (enforced by * separator).

Note

Credentials are discovered automatically from environment variables, config files, or IAM/ADC. The SDK never accepts explicit credential parameters.

docs.title: Publishing Messages
docs.text:
from multicloud.pubsub import TopicClient, Message

with TopicClient(provider="aws", topic_name="orders", region="us-west-2") as client:
    # Build and send a message
    message = (
        Message.builder()
        .with_body(b'{"order_id": "12345", "amount": 99.99}')
        .with_metadata("content-type", "application/json")
        .with_metadata("priority", "high")
        .build()
    )

    client.send(message)

docs.title: Building Messages
docs.text:
Use the builder pattern to construct messages:

message = (
    Message.builder()
    .with_body("Hello World")  # Accepts str or bytes
    .with_metadata("key1", "value1")
    .with_metadata("key2", "value2")
    .build()
)

# Or provide metadata as a dict
message = (
    Message.builder()
    .with_body(b"Binary data")
    .with_metadata({
        "content-type": "application/octet-stream",
        "version": "1.0"
    })
    .build()
)

docs.title: Receiving Messages
docs.text:
from multicloud.pubsub import SubscriptionClient

with SubscriptionClient(provider="aws", subscription_name="orders-processor", region="us-west-2") as client:
    # Receive a message
    message = client.receive()

    try:
        # Process the message
        process_order(message.body)

        # Acknowledge successful processing
        client.send_ack(message.ack_id)
    except Exception as e:
        # Negative acknowledge on failure (returns to queue)
        client.send_nack(message.ack_id)

docs.title: Batch Acknowledgments
docs.text:
Process and acknowledge multiple messages efficiently:

with SubscriptionClient(provider="aws", subscription_name="orders") as client:
    messages = []

    # Receive multiple messages
    for _ in range(10):
        msg = client.receive()
        messages.append(msg)

    # Process all messages
    results = process_batch(messages)

    # Batch acknowledge
    successful_ids = [msg.ack_id for msg, success in zip(messages, results) if success]
    failed_ids = [msg.ack_id for msg, success in zip(messages, results) if not success]

    client.send_acks(successful_ids)
    client.send_nacks(failed_ids)

docs.title: Negative Acknowledgment with Visibility Timeout
docs.text:
Control when a failed message becomes visible again:

from datetime import timedelta

with SubscriptionClient(provider="aws", subscription_name="orders") as client:
    message = client.receive()

    try:
        process_message(message.body)
        client.send_ack(message.ack_id)
    except RetryableError:
        # Return to queue, invisible for 60 seconds
        client.send_nack(
            message.ack_id,
            visibility_timeout=timedelta(seconds=60)
        )

docs.title: Subscription Attributes
docs.text:
with SubscriptionClient(provider="aws", subscription_name="orders") as client:
    attrs = client.get_attributes()
    print(f"Approximate messages: {attrs.approximate_number_of_messages}")

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
All pub/sub operations raise exceptions from the common multicloud.common.exceptions hierarchy:

from multicloud.pubsub import TopicClient, Message
from multicloud.common.exceptions import (
    ResourceNotFoundException,
    InvalidArgumentException,
    UnAuthorizedException,
    SubstrateSdkException,
)

with TopicClient(provider="aws", topic_name="orders", region="us-west-2") as client:
    try:
        message = Message.builder().with_body(b"data").build()
        client.send(message)
    except ResourceNotFoundException as e:
        print(f"Topic not found: {e}")
    except UnAuthorizedException as e:
        print(f"Access denied: {e}")
    except SubstrateSdkException as e:
        print(f"SDK error: {e}")
Exception When Raised ResourceNotFoundException Topic or subscription does not exist InvalidArgumentException Empty body, invalid metadata, bad visibility timeout UnAuthorizedException Credentials missing, expired, or insufficient FailedPreconditionException Client shutdown, batch handler error UnknownException Unmapped provider error

docs.title: Switching Providers
docs.text:
Change providers by modifying only the provider parameter:

# AWS
with TopicClient(provider="aws", topic_name="orders", region="us-west-2") as client:
    client.send(message)

# GCP
with TopicClient(provider="gcp", topic_name="orders", region="us-central1") as client:
    client.send(message)

# Ali
with TopicClient(provider="ali", topic_name="orders", region="cn-hangzhou") as client:
    client.send(message)

The rest of your code remains identical — the SDK handles all provider-specific differences.

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
A full round-trip: publish, receive, acknowledge.

from multicloud.pubsub import TopicClient, SubscriptionClient, Message

# Publish a message
with TopicClient(provider="aws", topic_name="orders", region="us-west-2") as publisher:
    message = (
        Message.builder()
        .with_body(b'{"order_id": "12345", "amount": 99.99}')
        .with_metadata("content-type", "application/json")
        .build()
    )
    publisher.send(message)
    print("Message published")

# Receive and process
with SubscriptionClient(provider="aws", subscription_name="orders-processor", region="us-west-2") as subscriber:
    message = subscriber.receive()
    print(f"Received: {message.body.decode()}")

    # Process and acknowledge
    process_order(message.body)
    subscriber.send_ack(message.ack_id)
    print("Message acknowledged")

docs.title: Client Lifecycle
docs.text:
Both TopicClient and SubscriptionClient support the context manager protocol:

# Preferred — automatic cleanup and batch flushing
with TopicClient(provider="aws", topic_name="orders", region="us-west-2") as client:
    client.send(message)

# Manual cleanup
client = TopicClient(provider="aws", topic_name="orders", region="us-west-2")
try:
    client.send(message)
finally:
    client.close()  # Flushes pending batches

docs.title: Security Token Service (STS) Guide
docs.text: The STS module provides cloud-agnostic identity and credential management. Use it to verify caller identity, assume roles for cross-account access, exchange federated (OIDC) tokens, and mint access or service-account tokens. A companion StsUtilities class signs identity requests offline for cloud-native auth brokers.

docs.title: Creating a Client
docs.text:
from multicloud.sts import StsClient

# AWS
with StsClient(provider="aws", region="us-west-2") as sts:
    ...

# Google Cloud
with StsClient(provider="gcp") as sts:
    ...

docs.title: Constructor Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Description provider str ✅ Provider id: "aws" or "gcp" region str Region, interpreted per provider (not required for GCP) endpoint str Endpoint URL override properties Mapping[str, Any] Provider-specific extras passed through to the provider

All parameters are keyword-only (enforced by * separator).

docs.title: With a Custom Endpoint
docs.text:
with StsClient(
    provider="aws",
    region="us-west-2",
    endpoint="https://sts.us-west-2.amazonaws.com",
) as sts:
    ...

Note

Credentials are discovered automatically from environment variables, config files, or IAM/ADC. The SDK never accepts explicit credential parameters in the constructor.

docs.title: Getting Caller Identity
docs.text:
Retrieve identity information for the currently authenticated principal.

from multicloud.sts import StsClient

with StsClient(provider="aws", region="us-west-2") as sts:
    identity = sts.get_caller_identity()
    print(f"Account:  {identity.account_id}")
    print(f"Resource: {identity.cloud_resource_name}")
    print(f"User ID:  {identity.user_id}")

get_caller_identity accepts an optional aud keyword; some providers use it for audience-scoped identity tokens, others ignore it.

The returned CallerIdentity is a frozen dataclass:

Field Type Description user_id str Unique identifier of the calling entity cloud_resource_name str Cloud resource identifier / identity proof account_id str Cloud account/project that owns the identity

docs.title: Assuming a Role
docs.text:
Assume a role and receive temporary credentials for cross-account or elevated-privilege access. Returns an StsCredentials.

from multicloud.sts import StsClient

with StsClient(provider="aws", region="us-west-2") as sts:
    creds = sts.assume_role(
        "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/CrossAccountRole",
        session_name="my-session",
        expiration=3600,
    )
    print(f"Access Key ID: {creds.access_key_id}")
    print(f"Token:         {creds.security_token}")
    print(f"Expires:       {creds.expiration}")

docs.title: Assume Role Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description role str ✅ Cloud resource name to assume session_name str Session identifier; an SDK default is applied when empty expiration int Duration in seconds; default 3600 (must be positive) external_id str External ID for cross-account access policy str Inline policy to scope down permissions tags Mapping[str, str] Session tags credential_scope CredentialScope Optional scope to downscope the returned credentials

docs.title: StsCredentials Fields
docs.text:
StsCredentials is a frozen dataclass returned by all credential operations. Which fields are populated depends on the operation and provider; provider-agnostic code should rely on security_token (and expiration when present).

Field Type Description access_key_id str Access key identifier, or empty for bearer/token-only credentials access_key_secret str Secret access key, or empty for bearer/token-only credentials security_token str Session/bearer token (always populated) expiration datetime \| None When the credentials expire, or None if the provider reports none

docs.title: Federated Sign-In (Web Identity)
docs.text:
Exchange a web identity (OIDC/JWT) token minted by an external identity provider for short-lived cloud credentials — no long-lived cloud keys required.

from multicloud.sts import StsClient

with StsClient(provider="aws", region="us-west-2") as sts:
    creds = sts.assume_role_with_web_identity(
        "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/WebIdentityRole",
        web_identity_token=oidc_jwt,
        session_name="federated-session",
        expiration=3600,
    )
    print(creds.security_token)

docs.title: Web Identity Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Description role str ✅ Cloud resource identifier to assume (interpreted per provider) web_identity_token str ✅ OIDC/JWT token proving external identity session_name str Session identifier (provider support varies) expiration int Requested duration in seconds; default 3600 (provider support varies)

On AWS this maps to AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity. On GCP it performs an RFC 8693 token exchange via Workload Identity Federation; the federated access token is returned in security_token.

docs.title: Getting an Access Token
docs.text:
Retrieve a fresh access token. Pass audience for an audience-scoped token or scopes for an OAuth-scoped token — the two are mutually exclusive.

from multicloud.sts import StsClient

with StsClient(provider="gcp") as sts:
    # OAuth-scoped token
    token = sts.get_access_token(
        scopes=["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    )

    # ...or an audience-scoped token
    token = sts.get_access_token(audience="my-target-audience")

    print(token.security_token)

docs.title: Access Token Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Description audience str Target audience for an audience-scoped token (mutually exclusive with scopes) scopes list[str] OAuth scopes for a scoped token (mutually exclusive with audience) duration_seconds int Requested duration; providers may cap or ignore it

Note

audience and scopes are GCP-only parameters. The AWS implementation of get_access_token maps to GetSessionToken, which does not support either parameter — both are silently ignored when calling with provider="aws".

docs.title: Service Account Tokens
docs.text:
Generate a token for a target service account via impersonation.

from multicloud.sts import StsClient

with StsClient(provider="gcp") as sts:
    token = sts.generate_service_account_token(
        "my-sa@my-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
        scopes=["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"],
        lifetime=3600,
    )
    print(token.security_token)

docs.title: Service Account Token Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Description target_principal str ✅ Service account to impersonate (format per provider) scopes list[str] ✅ OAuth scopes to request on the generated token lifetime int Token lifetime in seconds; default 3600 (range/behaviour per provider)

Note

generate_service_account_token is supported on GCP. On AWS it raises UnsupportedOperationException.

docs.title: Signed Auth Requests (Cloud-Native Auth)
docs.text:
StsUtilities is a companion to StsClient for offline request signing. Instead of calling the provider itself, it produces a signed-but-unsent identity request. You hand that request to another system — typically an identity broker such as HashiCorp Vault's AWS-IAM auth method — which replays it to the provider to verify who you are, then issues its own token or secret in return.

from multicloud.sts.sts_client import StsUtilities

with StsUtilities(provider="aws", region="us-west-2") as utils:
    signed = utils.create_signed_auth_request(
        # Extra headers are folded into the signature, so the broker can
        # bind them to the verified identity (e.g. Vault's server-id header).
        custom_headers={"X-Vault-AWS-IAM-Server-ID": "vault.example.com"},
    )

    # Forward these fields to the broker; it replays the request as-is.
    print(signed.method)   # "POST"
    print(signed.url)      # the provider's identity endpoint
    print(signed.headers)  # includes the signature and any custom headers
    print(signed.body)     # request body bytes

On AWS this signs a GetCallerIdentity request with SigV4 using the caller's discovered credentials; the SDK never sends that request itself — replaying it is the broker's job. Resolving the signing credentials can still require a network call (an assume_role/web-identity overrider, or an IMDS/SSO chain, is fetched lazily at signing time); only static credentials sign with zero network I/O. Because custom_headers are part of the signed headers, the broker can trust that a value like X-Vault-AWS-IAM-Server-ID was bound at signing time and not injected during replay.

docs.title: Constructor Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Description provider str ✅ Provider id: "aws" region str Region, interpreted per provider; required by AWS for signing credentials_overrider CredentialsOverrider Override default credential resolution properties Mapping[str, Any] Provider-specific extras passed through to the provider

All parameters are keyword-only.

docs.title: create_signed_auth_request Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description custom_headers Mapping[str, str] Extra headers folded into the signature so a broker can bind them to the identity

docs.title: SignedAuthRequest Fields
docs.text:
SignedAuthRequest is a frozen dataclass — the signed request to forward to the broker.

Field Type Description method str HTTP method of the signed request url str Fully-qualified request URL headers Mapping[str, str] Signed request headers (single value per name); replayable identity proof — treat as a secret body bytes Request body bytes credentials StsCredentials Signer identity (key id + session token); the long-term signing secret is omitted

Note

create_signed_auth_request is supported on AWS. On GCP it raises UnsupportedOperationException — GCP has no equivalent client-signed identity request.

docs.title: Provider Support
docs.text: Operation AWS GCP get_caller_identity Yes Yes assume_role Yes Yes assume_role_with_web_identity Yes Yes get_access_token Yes (ignores audience and scopes) Yes generate_service_account_token No (UnsupportedOperationException) Yes StsUtilities.create_signed_auth_request Yes No (UnsupportedOperationException)

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
A full round-trip: verify the current identity, assume a role, and inspect the temporary credentials.

from multicloud.sts import StsClient

with StsClient(provider="aws", region="us-west-2") as sts:
    # Verify current identity
    identity = sts.get_caller_identity()
    print(f"Caller: {identity.cloud_resource_name}")

    # Assume a cross-account role
    creds = sts.assume_role(
        "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/CrossAccountRole",
        session_name="demo",
        expiration=900,
    )

    # Use the temporary credentials
    assert creds.security_token
    print(f"Assumed role; token expires: {creds.expiration}")

docs.title: Switching Providers
docs.text:
The same code works across clouds — change only the provider (and region where applicable):

from multicloud.sts import StsClient

providers = [
    {"provider": "aws", "region": "us-west-2"},
    {"provider": "gcp"},
]

for config in providers:
    with StsClient(**config) as sts:
        identity = sts.get_caller_identity()
        print(f"[{config['provider']}] Account: {identity.account_id}")

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
All STS operations raise exceptions from the common multicloud.common.exceptions hierarchy:

from multicloud.sts import StsClient
from multicloud.common.exceptions import (
    UnAuthorizedException,
    InvalidArgumentException,
    UnsupportedOperationException,
    SubstrateSdkException,
)

with StsClient(provider="aws", region="us-west-2") as sts:
    try:
        creds = sts.assume_role(
            "arn:aws:iam::999:role/DoesNotExist",
            session_name="test",
        )
    except UnAuthorizedException as e:
        print(f"Not authorized: {e}")
    except InvalidArgumentException as e:
        print(f"Bad input: {e}")
    except SubstrateSdkException as e:
        print(f"SDK error: {e}")

STS operations map provider errors onto this subset of the common multicloud.common.exceptions hierarchy:

Exception When Raised UnAuthorizedException Credentials missing/expired, insufficient permissions, or the target role cannot be assumed (e.g. missing or denied) InvalidArgumentException Invalid parameters (e.g. empty role, non-positive duration, both audience and scopes) UnsupportedOperationException Operation not supported by the provider (e.g. generate_service_account_token on AWS) UnknownException Unmapped provider error

Other exception types in the common hierarchy (such as ResourceNotFoundException) are not currently emitted by STS operations; catch SubstrateSdkException for a provider-agnostic catch-all.

docs.title: Client Lifecycle
docs.text:
StsClient supports the context manager protocol for deterministic cleanup:

# Preferred — automatic cleanup
with StsClient(provider="aws", region="us-west-2") as sts:
    identity = sts.get_caller_identity()

# Manual cleanup
sts = StsClient(provider="aws", region="us-west-2")
try:
    identity = sts.get_caller_identity()
finally:
    sts.close()

docs.title: Releasing MultiCloud Python
docs.text: All 21 multicloud-py-* distributions share the version in VERSION and are released together under one multicloud-py-v* tag.

docs.title: How the release version is chosen
docs.text:
We use Release Please to open and maintain a release pull request after changes are merged to main. It is the release automation project maintained by the googleapis GitHub organization.

The version-increment policy is provided by Release Please's built-in DefaultVersioningStrategy, not by custom Python SDK code. Our release-please-config.json selects the simple file-update strategy, specifies the multicloud-py tag component, and tells Release Please to update VERSION; it does not override the version-increment policy.

The version line in VERSION carries Release Please's required x-release-please-version annotation. Repository scripts parse only the semantic version before that annotation, while Release Please uses the marker to update the file in every generated release PR.

Change merged since the last release Commit convention Result from 0.1.4 Backward-compatible bug fix fix: ... 0.1.5 Backward-compatible capability feat: ... 0.2.0 Breaking public API change feat!: ... or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer 1.0.0

Release Please calculates the largest required increment among the commits since the previous release. It records the last released version in .release-please-manifest.json, then proposes the next version in a release PR. The release configuration uses include-component-in-tag and include-v-in-tag, so version 0.1.4 produces the Git tag multicloud-py-v0.1.4.

The same default applies before 1.0.0: 0.9.9 becomes 0.9.10 for a patch, 0.10.0 for a feature, and 1.0.0 for a breaking change. Reaching 0.9.9 does not itself trigger a major release.

Use Release-As: X.Y.Z in a commit footer only when intentionally overriding the calculated version, such as the initial 0.1.4 bootstrap release. Do not manually edit the manifest for an ordinary release.

After Release Please updates VERSION, the sync-release-pr job runs scripts/sync_version.py and uv lock on the generated release branch. This propagates the selected version to every distribution's pyproject.toml, inter-package dependency constraints, and lock file before the release PR is reviewed.

docs.title: One-time administrator setup
docs.text:
1. In GitHub Actions settings, allow workflows to create pull requests and grant read/write workflow permissions. Release Please and the synchronization job use the repository GITHUB_TOKEN; do not add a personal access token or GitHub App credential.
  2. Create one protected GitHub environment per distribution, with the required release reviewers. The publishing workflows use testpypi-<distribution-name> for TestPyPI and pypi-<distribution-name> for production PyPI. Each production PyPI project must trust workflow release.yml with its matching pypi-<distribution-name> environment.
  3. TestPyPI permits only three pending Trusted Publishers at a time. Register the three distributions in one bootstrap batch with owner salesforce, repository multicloud-py, workflow test-pypi.yml, and environment testpypi-<distribution-name>. Run TestPyPI Rehearsal for that batch; successful publication converts those three entries to active publishers and frees three pending slots. Repeat for all seven batches before the complete TestPyPI installation rehearsal.
  4. Require the normal pull-request CI workflow on main.

docs.title: Normal release process
docs.text:
The maintainer-facing process intentionally matches MultiCloudJ:

  1. Merge conventional commits to main.
  2. Release Please opens or updates one release PR. The synchronization job updates all 21 package manifests and uv.lock on that branch.
  3. Review the release PR and ensure its normal CI checks pass.
  4. Merge the release PR. No separate publishing workflow needs to be started.
  5. The same release.yml run creates the Git tag and GitHub release, builds 21 wheels and 21 sdists, runs the unit and replay-mode conformance suites, validates metadata and licenses, and installs each wheel independently.
  6. Only after validation succeeds, the workflow publishes the exact validated artifacts through the 21 pypi-<distribution-name> environments. The release run remains in progress until every PyPI project finishes, and it fails if any publication fails.

The release-main concurrency group serializes the complete process, including publication. PyPI and TestPyPI versions are immutable. The publisher uses PyPI's duplicate-skipping support so a failed matrix job can be rerun without re-uploading an artifact that already succeeded. Rerun only failed jobs; never delete or overwrite published artifacts.

docs.title: Migrating the production Trusted Publishers to release.yml
docs.text:
The retained production projects were initially created with bootstrap-pypi.yml. Before merging the next release PR, update each of the 18 retained PyPI projects under Manage → Publishing:

  • Owner: salesforce
  • Repository: multicloud-py
  • Workflow: release.yml
  • Environment: pypi-<distribution-name>

Add the release.yml publisher first, then remove the old bootstrap-pypi.yml publisher.

The three new Ali distributions require these exact registrations:

Distribution Production workflow Production environment Test workflow Test environment multicloud-py-blob-ali release.yml pypi-multicloud-py-blob-ali test-pypi.yml testpypi-multicloud-py-blob-ali multicloud-py-pubsub-ali release.yml pypi-multicloud-py-pubsub-ali test-pypi.yml testpypi-multicloud-py-pubsub-ali multicloud-py-sts-ali release.yml pypi-multicloud-py-sts-ali test-pypi.yml testpypi-multicloud-py-sts-ali

Keep release PR #10 unmerged until these three new production publishers and all 18 retained production publishers trust release.yml. Existing TestPyPI publishers continue using test-pypi.yml; only the three new Ali projects need new TestPyPI registrations.

docs.title: Maintaining the website
docs.text:
The documentation website uses MkDocs Material. Markdown sources live on main in docs/, navigation and rendering settings in mkdocs.yml, and locked tooling in the docs dependency group in pyproject.toml and uv.lock.

GitHub Pages serves generated HTML from the site branch's /docs folder, matching the publishing-source layout used by MultiCloudJ. The Documentation Actions workflow validates source builds; it does not deploy the website.

docs.title: Preview and validate
docs.text:
From the repository root:

uv run --frozen --group docs mkdocs serve
uv run --frozen --group docs mkdocs build --strict

Use the preview URL printed by MkDocs. The default build writes to the ignored site/ directory. API reference pages are generated from source docstrings with mkdocstrings; planning documents under docs/superpowers/ are excluded. Do not commit generated output to main or replace its Markdown docs/ tree.

docs.title: Publish a new version
docs.text:
First merge documentation or SDK changes into main. Build from that merged commit in a clean checkout or isolated worktree; preserve existing local work. Use a fresh temporary build directory and a separate publishing worktree.

The following commands assume origin is the public repository and an existing site branch has already been initialized. Run them in a dedicated shell and keep that shell open through review and submission so the variables remain available. Fail-fast mode prevents a failed build from reaching publication.

set -e
git fetch origin main site
SOURCE_SHA=$(git rev-parse origin/main)
BUILD_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
SOURCE_DIR=$(mktemp -d)/source
PUBLISH_DIR=$(mktemp -d)/publish
PUBLISH_BRANCH="codex/publish-site-$(git rev-parse --short origin/main)-$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)"

git worktree add --detach "$SOURCE_DIR" "$SOURCE_SHA"
(cd "$SOURCE_DIR" && uv run --frozen --group docs mkdocs build --strict --site-dir "$BUILD_DIR")

git worktree add -b "$PUBLISH_BRANCH" "$PUBLISH_DIR" origin/site
# This isolated worktree contains generated website files only.
git -C "$PUBLISH_DIR" rm -r --ignore-unmatch docs
mkdir -p "$PUBLISH_DIR/docs"
cp -R "$BUILD_DIR/." "$PUBLISH_DIR/docs/"
touch "$PUBLISH_DIR/docs/.nojekyll"
git -C "$PUBLISH_DIR" add docs
git -C "$PUBLISH_DIR" diff --cached --check

Review the complete generated change, verify the homepage and at least one API page, and confirm that obsolete generated pages are removed. If the staged diff is empty, no publish is needed. Otherwise:

git -C "$PUBLISH_DIR" commit -m "docs: publish site from $SOURCE_SHA"
git -C "$PUBLISH_DIR" push origin "$PUBLISH_BRANCH"
gh pr create --repo salesforce/multicloud-py --base site --head "$PUBLISH_BRANCH" \
  --title "docs: publish website" \
  --body "Publishes the strict MkDocs build from main commit $SOURCE_SHA."

If you cannot create branches upstream, push to your fork remote instead of origin and use --head "OWNER:$PUBLISH_BRANCH" when opening the PR, replacing OWNER with the fork owner's GitHub login.

After the publishing PR merges into site, GitHub Pages deploys its /docs folder. .nojekyll makes Pages serve the generated files without a Jekyll transformation. No force-push or mkdocs gh-deploy is needed. Use normal Git worktree cleanup after retaining any needed review artifacts.

docs.title: One-time switch from Actions deployment
docs.text:
1. Merge the change that removes artifact deployment from the Documentation workflow. Wait for any older in-flight Actions deployments to finish.
  2. Initialize site with the validated static build in /docs, including /docs/.nojekyll, if that branch does not yet exist.
  3. In repository Settings → Pages, choose Deploy from a branch, select site, select /docs, and save.
  4. Check the Pages build and the public homepage and guides. Enable Enforce HTTPS when available.

The canonical URL remains https://opensource.salesforce.com/multicloud-py/. The organization domain is inherited; leave the repository custom-domain field empty and do not add a CNAME for opensource.salesforce.com.

Verify the configuration and deployment with:

gh api repos/salesforce/multicloud-py/pages
gh api repos/salesforce/multicloud-py/pages/builds/latest

The configuration should report build_type: legacy and source branch site, path /docs. GitHub may display its own Pages build as an Actions run even with this branch-based setting; it is separate from our validation workflow.
